# Constrained Native Muscle Moco and Excitation Replay

Issue #12143 adds a versioned OpenSim 4.6 diagnostic for a declared constrained
cold start, native muscle excitation, and independent same-input replay. It
extends the preparation recipe in chapter 41 and the maintained offline Moco
runner in chapter 39. The original fixed-path muscle bundle retains its
stricter component policy. This calculation does not certify anatomy,
physiology, contact, grip, or a captured golf swing.

## Native State and Input Contract

The caller supplies an unchanged self-contained `.osim` entrypoint SHA-256,
every native named continuous state, time zero, exact model-owned lock targets,
constraint enforcement flags, coordinate chart bounds, and a residual
tolerance. Native `initSystem()` may assemble its default state. The owned
preparation then applies declared lock targets and restores the frozen named
state without further assembly or muscle equilibration. The policy binds the
loaded native model, provider source, registered modeling options, muscle
state schema, excitation channel order, interpolation, exact knots, and
declared constraint/chart rules to a T01 experiment-replay bundle. Source
XML entrypoint hashing does not imply a transitive resource closure.

For each admitted muscle $i$, a native time-only player applies saved
excitation $e_i(t)$ by linear interpolation of the exact Moco control knots.
The native muscle law evolves activation and fiber state internally. A fresh
source load and one uninterrupted Runge–Kutta–Merson integration produce
$x_k^{\mathrm{replay}}$ at every declared knot $t_k$. The replay compares
the native applied excitation with the saved channel values and observes
position and velocity constraint errors and source charts at each knot.
Native constraint reactions are plant outputs, never injected controls.
The scorer samples declared source-frame marker placements from restored
replayed states without reassembly or a second integration.

The `declared-constrained-muscles/2.0.0` profile admits exact native
coordinate couplers, a one-coordinate unit-linear `CustomJoint` rotation
chart, and simple fixed or coordinate-linear moving path points. Moving
path coordinates require declared chart bounds; native function coefficients
must be finite. Source-byte identity binds the actual coefficients and path
route. Nonlinear moving-point laws, conditional points, wraps, external or
non-muscle forces, source controllers, prescribed motion, and contact remain
outside this profile. Native moving-guide work is retained as modeled; no
workless-guide or anatomical interpretation is inferred.

## Moco Feasibility Versus Replay Agreement

The maintained file request may carry this exact constrained cold-start
declaration. Preparation collects independent blockers before solving and
checks T01 replay capability with the same declared source and state.
OpenSim 4.6 Moco rejects locked coordinates at solver initialization; a
locked-source replay capability therefore does **not** authorize a locked
Moco solve or topology transformation. A coupler-only source can enter Moco.

The native two-Millard, three-joint fixture has an active coupler
$q_d=2q$, nonzero muscle forces, and a requested independent-coordinate
displacement of $5\times10^{-6}$ rad over 10 ms. With 10 mesh intervals,
convergence tolerance $10^{-6}$, constraint tolerance $10^{-7}$, and a
300-iteration cap, Moco reaches its final-state bound. Its exact saved
control knots replay on a fresh native model. Maximum transcription-to-replay
differences at the returned 21 knots were $1.935\times10^{-7}$ rad for
coordinates, $3.827\times10^{-9}$ rad/s for speeds,
$1.647\times10^{-11}$ for activation, and $4.994\times10^{-9}$ m for
fiber length. Position and velocity constraint residuals remain below the
declared $10^{-9}$ tolerance. Fixture-specific tests require coordinate
error below $2\times10^{-7}$ rad and final replay target error below that
same bound. These measured differences are separate from optimizer success
and from capture-observation accuracy.

An earlier zero-force path fixture let a loose $10^{-4}$ transcription
tolerance meet a tiny endpoint despite almost zero native speed; its fresh
replay did not follow that endpoint. It was rejected as positive matching
evidence. The revised source geometry produces nonzero native force and
motion. This failure is retained as a reason for strict native replay
acceptance after every solve, rather than trusting transcription status.

## Remaining Scientific Gates

The unchanged 520-muscle source still lacks approved private marker
attachments/registration, source-anatomy and passive-load resolution,
mechanical-assistance exclusion, exact contact/grip and constraint policy,
and complete bounded native state preparation. The locked-coordinate Moco
limitation requires a separate source-faithful reduction with native
body/path/force equivalence; stock weld replacement cannot be assumed to
preserve nonzero lock targets or actuator references. No blocked production
solve is run. The required full-horizon muscular OpenSim excitation replay,
all 17 variants, and six-engine comparison denominator remain open.
